subject: science
passage: The platypus, an egg-laying mammal of eastern Australia, hunts along the bottoms of streams with its eyes, ears, and nostrils tightly closed. It finds food using its soft, rubbery bill, which is covered with tens of thousands of tiny sensors. Some of these sensors respond to touch, while others pick up the weak electric signals given off by the muscles of moving prey such as shrimp and insect larvae.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how the platypus locates prey without using its eyes
choices.B: To describe the shrimp and insect larvae that live in Australian streams
choices.C: To compare the platypus with other mammals that lay eggs
choices.D: To argue that the platypus is the most skilled hunter in Australian streams

explanation.why: The first sentence sets up a puzzle: the platypus hunts "with its eyes, ears, and nostrils tightly closed." The rest of the text answers it by explaining that sensors on the bill detect touch and the "weak electric signals" of prey. So the text mainly explains how the platypus finds food without sight.
explanation.A: Correct. The text explains that the platypus closes its eyes underwater and relies on touch and electric sensors in its bill to find prey.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Shrimp and insect larvae are named only as examples of prey; the text does not describe them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text mentions that the platypus lays eggs but never compares it with any other egg-laying mammal.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text explains how the platypus hunts; it never ranks it against other hunters, so this claims far more than the text does.
